description: A pocket-sized King Street institution with wood-panelled Victorian rooms, etched rowing windows and a buzz of student and local regulars. Named for a Thames sculling champion who insisted his mail be sent to King Street, it remains on the notorious King Street Run and hosts an annual cricket match against St Radegund. CAMRA Cambridgeshire Pub of the Year 2024, the Champ pours immaculate Greene King and guest ales alongside pork pies, scotch eggs and Sunday cheese and crackers in a nationally listed historic interior.

Set on Trumpington High Street, this Grade II listed medieval timber frame hides behind later brickwork yet still feels like a proper country pub on the edge of Cambridge. Mitchells & Butlers runs a food-led house with an open-plan bar, high-roofed restaurant and a garden seating around two hundred. Adnams Broadside and Sharp's Doom Bar anchor the taps while extensive menus run from weekend breakfasts to Sunday roasts, making it as much a dining destination as a pint stop after a riverside walk.

A handsome village local in Swaffham Prior pours well-kept cask ales for walkers and cyclists exploring the Cambridgeshire fens. Expect a straightforward welcome, traditional bar furnishings and a beer garden suited to summer afternoons. The pub trades as a community anchor for the parish, with food and events that draw locals from across the CB25 villages between Newmarket and Cambridge.

Linton's High Street Dog & Duck pairs exposed beams and a warm village atmosphere with real ale from regional brewers. A favourite stop on the Granta valley pub trail, it mixes locals, visitors to the nearby racecourse and walkers heading into the chalk hills. Expect honest pub food, a garden for sunny days and the easy-going rhythm of a small South Cambridgeshire free house.

Burwell's Fox occupies a prominent spot in one of East Cambridgeshire's largest villages, serving cask beers and hearty pub cooking to fenland regulars and visitors to the nearby museum and nature reserves. The bar mixes sport on screen with a relaxed dining room, while seasonal menus and weekend roasts keep tables busy. A dependable stop after exploring the Cambridgeshire levels.

Milton's White Horse is a roomy village pub on the High Street with a broad beer garden, family-friendly dining and Sky sport for match days. Keg and cask lines include local Milton Brewery beers, and the kitchen turns out grills, burgers and Sunday roasts in a bright, modernised interior. Handy for the science park crowd as well as Milton residents looking for an unpretentious local.

Bottisham's Bell is a classic chalk-country inn with low beams, open fires and a reputation for well-kept Greene King and guest ales. Lunchtime and evening menus lean on British pub staples, while the garden catches the afternoon sun after walks on the B1102. A settled village local midway between Cambridge and Newmarket that rewards a detour from the A14.

Tucked at the top of King Street, Cambridge's smallest pub reopened in early 2026 as a cosy, community-driven cask house after years of uncertainty. House beers Sackcloth and Habit Ale build on Milton ales, joined by London Pride and rotating SIBA guests on a handful of handpumps. Memorabilia from the legendary King Street Run and the pub's cricket and rowing clubs lines the walls in a space where every seat feels like the regulars' table.
